mappings.notes: CHAIN BRIDGING ROW, per the adopted R2 bridging convention (adopted 26fo, verified 26fp) -- NOT THIS MEMBER'S WORK, disclosed, and the same device every delta since the carve has used for its own predecessor. base_revision here is 19568143, the PREDECESSOR MANIFEST'S DECLARED new_revision, so the validator's CHAIN abutment check composes. Under the convention's 'manifest names its parent' pattern the surface pass's manifest-finalization commit (c5a52ab, which created this file) and its staging merge (37fe960, this branch's real base) fall OUTSIDE the range that predecessor declares, so they land inside this delta's range instead. `git diff --name-status --no-renames 19568143 37fe960` is exactly this one added path and nothing else. Without this row check (4) COVERAGE would fail on an add this member did not make.

THE R2-TIP CUMULATIVE MANIFEST -- the KB-consumption artifact for the successor-locator pass, and the reason this member exists. It declares base_revision 9288e01ab337626ea4c7bbe5518885e93a244460 and new_revision 19568143c396998b00f02d585caa66c9cf884297, composing the five committed deltas into 50 rows over 253 base->tip path pairs. READ THE WINDOW BOUNDARY BEFORE VALIDATING: the cumulative spans the R2 CODE window and STOPS at 19568143. This delta's own range is bookkeeping -- docs and manifests, zero cablp code paths -- and is deliberately OUTSIDE it. The gate invocation of record is therefore the FIVE code deltas plus the cumulative; adding THIS delta to that invocation asks a different question and correctly reports a CHAIN window mismatch, because the cumulative does not span this delta's commits. Both CHAIN findings that a six-manifest run emits are true: the window one names the cause, and the composition one fires alongside it only because this particular delta happens to carry same-path rows on the files it modifies. A bookkeeping delta whose rows were all `add` would compose identically and leave the window check as the ONLY thing standing between a wrong window and a green run -- which is why that check now exists (see the validate_manifest.py row below). A cumulative that is wanted for a LATER tip is re-cut at that tip; it is never widened by assertion.

THE GATE'S OWN CONTRACT, WIDENED. Check (3) previously compared path pairs only, so a cumulative could declare the wrong end of the window and still pass every check whenever the deltas it omitted moved no file -- which is exactly a surface or docstring delta, the kind that closes an R2 phase. `check_chain` now additionally asserts that the cumulative's base_revision is the first delta's and its new_revision is the last delta's, and it refuses more than one cumulative rather than silently composing against the first and leaving the rest unchecked. Its signature takes the cumulative LIST rather than one manifest for that second reason. Three self-test cases added, each built so exactly one check fires: fail-CHAIN-window-tip, fail-CHAIN-window-base, fail-CHAIN-two-cumulatives; the synthetic fixture repository grows two modify-only commits (root->base, tip->tail) so that a delta which legitimately moves nothing exists to build them from. 21/21 -> 24/24. The module docstring's statement of check (3) is updated in the same edit -- it is the executable statement of the schema constraints and must not lag them. NOTHING ELSE IN THE VALIDATOR CHANGED: no check was relaxed, no fixture retuned, and the chain half was made to RUN for the first time rather than made to pass.
